assertion_analysis.failure_condition: The error omits the modified member or expected fixed reason, or refusal writes links or stamps the anchor; removing each documented refusal instead prevents the expected exception and fails line 58.
The quarantine refusal omits the fixed member name, or removal of the refusal permits finalization and triggers pytest.fail; negative-control.log demonstrates the latter.
Preview errors, omits ready or the fixed count of two missing reverse pairs, or writes links.
Finalize errors, omits stamped or zero-call output, misses either shared-logger invocation, leaves an audit-detected missing reverse, or misses either fixed reciprocal link.
A stored signature differs from group_signature of the same fixture rows; a regression inside group_signature itself moves both sides together, so this assertion cannot catch it.
The independent planner returns another family count, decision other than harmonized, or nonzero calls after stamping.
An incomplete stamp is not refused with its member named, or the unstamped fixture member gains a signature; stamp-negative-control.log shows the missing-readback mutation reddens.
The pre-existing planner begins counting a null-stamped member and returns nonzero calls; this assertion documents the planner gap rather than guarding finalization.
The CLI succeeds for a quarantined fixture, fails to name the fixed member or reason, or writes links.

findings.text: blocking: reconcile_family_reverse_links writes writable members before returning its protected list; finalization raises only afterward at line 1464, so an approved member needing a reverse link can make --finalize fail after changing other members, while --dry-run reports ready.

follow-on: the test recomputes group_signature from the same fixture rows and function used to supply the stamp, so a regression that makes group_signature return the same wrong value on both sides leaves this current-signature assertion green.
